body:
### Summary

Improve performance of pointwise kernels by improving or eliminating per-point index
arithmetic and broadcast error paths that can trap on the GPU.

- **Linear multi-slab striding**: single-field property views (`data.ρ`) become linearly
  indexable via a constant-stride formula (one integer division per point instead of a full
  Cartesian decomposition), with allocation-free struct access in kernels.
- **Singleton broadcasting in point loops**: 0-dimensional and singleton-dimension layouts
  (e.g. surface fields) now broadcast like ordinary expressions. `each_slice_index` no longer 
  contains a kernel-reachable throw (the previous `DimensionMismatch` compiled into a device 
  trap that surfaced as `CUDA error: misaligned address (716)`). Genuine mismatches are rejected on the host. `IndexStyle` of a broadcast expression is linear only when its layouts share a shape,
  fixing silently wrong reductions over mixed-shape lazy expressions.
- **Linear point views**: `view_point_struct` reuses `array_and_index_args`, so the views
  built at every point of every broadcast argument use strided linear indices instead of
  converting linear → Cartesian (3 divisions per argument per point).
- **Single-launch reductions**: `reduce_points` on the GPU is one kernel launch using the
  last-block-done pattern, with the block results folded in registers by one warp (no
  second launch, no shared memory, so arbitrarily wide element types reduce at full
  bandwidth (`NTuple{16, Float64}`: +32%)). CPU reductions keep their documented pairwise
  accuracy and `@simd` vectorization.
- **Compacted masked loops**: `IJHMask` point and column loops iterate precomputed active
  indices instead of filtering every index against the mask, with coalesced access on GPUs.
  Masked launches are configured from unmasked upper bounds, so they no longer synchronize
  the stream to read the active count.

Adds `test/DataLayouts/benchmark_loops.jl` (CPU + GPU pipeline steps) covering broadcasts
and reductions over layouts, property views, and equal-/mixed-shape lazy expressions, plus
unit tests for singleton broadcasting and the host-side mismatch error.

CPU performance is at parity or better (broadcasts ~1.7× faster from unrolled slice
construction; mixed-shape lazy reductions ~25% faster); results are unchanged except where
mixed-shape reductions were previously wrong. Modest GPU performance gains.

---
## GPU Microbenchmarks: `ts/tail_effect` vs `main`

**Hardware**: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB · **Julia**: 1.11.9  
**Prognostic size**: `Nv = 63, Nq = 4, Nh = 5400` (~5.4M points)

*(Updated with `max_waves=1` explicitly applied)*

### Pointwise kernel bandwidth (`dest .= a .+ 2 .* b`)

| Layout | `main` | This PR | Change |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| 1-component `VIJFH` | 122.4 µs (994 GB/s) | **118.3 µs (1029 GB/s)** | +3.5% faster |
| Property-view `VIJFH` | 126.4 µs (963 GB/s) | **122.0 µs (997 GB/s)** | +3.6% faster |
| Raw `CuArray` reference | 119.4 µs (1019 GB/s) | 120.2 µs (1012 GB/s) | — |
| 1-comp overhead vs `CuArray` | 1.02× | **0.98×** | overhead eliminated |
| Prop-view overhead vs `CuArray` | 1.06× | **1.02×** | −4 pp |

### Scalar reduction (`sum(field)`)

| Domain size | `main` | This PR | Speedup |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `Nh = 50` (~50k points) | **47.8 µs** | 49.6 µs | 0.96× |
| `Nh = 500` (~504k points) | 55.1 µs | 55.0 µs | par |
| `Nh = 5400` (~5.4M points) | 90.1 µs | **87.5 µs** | **1.03×** |

Property-view reductions (`sum(field.a)`):

| Domain size | `main` | This PR | Speedup |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `Nh = 50` | **48.4 µs** | 49.7 µs | 0.97× |
| `Nh = 500` | 58.5 µs | **54.8 µs** | **1.07×** |
| `Nh = 5400` | 95.5 µs | **92.9 µs** | **1.03×** |

### Wide multi-component reduction bandwidth

`sum` of `NTuple{N, Float64}` at prognostic size. A100 `CuArray` ceiling ≈ 1019 GB/s.

| Eltype | `main` | This PR | Change |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `NTuple{1}` | 444 GB/s | **450 GB/s** | +1% |
| `NTuple{2}` | 617 GB/s | **670 GB/s** | **+9%** |
| `NTuple{4}` | 768 GB/s | **890 GB/s** | **+16%** |
| `NTuple{8}` | 936 GB/s | **1039 GB/s** | **+11%** |
| `NTuple{16}` | 1023 GB/s | **1119 GB/s** | **+9%** |

### Multi-component reduction time vs. raw `CUDA.mapreduce`

| Components | `main` | This PR | vs. `main` | vs. `CUDA.mapreduce` |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `Nf = 1` | 92.2 µs | **89.9 µs** | **1.03×** | 1.86× |
| `Nf = 2` | 131.8 µs | **122.1 µs** | **1.08×** | 2.22× |
| `Nf = 4` | 211.2 µs | **183.2 µs** | **1.15×** | 2.60× |

(`CUDA.mapreduce` on raw parent: ~167.4 µs, ~270.7 µs, ~476.0 µs for `Nf` = 1, 2, 4)

### Lazy broadcast reductions

| Expression | `main` | This PR | Speedup |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| `sum(a .+ b)` (equal shape) | 145.2 µs | **129.1 µs** | **1.12×** |
| `sum(a .+ surface)` (mixed shape) | 197.8 µs | **187.2 µs** | **1.06×** |

### Host-side kernel launch latency (tiny problem, isolates dispatch cost)

| Kernel | `main` | This PR | Notes |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---|
| Small broadcast | 18.1 µs | 18.7 µs | par |
| Small fill | 16.3 µs | 17.6 µs | par |
| Small `sum` (first call) | **39.3 µs** | 46.1 µs | +7 µs: task-local sync-counter init |
| Raw `CuArray` broadcast | 17.9 µs | 18.6 µs | par |

### Register Count Reduction (via CUDA.registers)

By simplifying the struct_index / parent_offset accessors and using CompactDeviceView, we successfully reduced register pressure in the primary GPU kernels.

main: 72 – 80 registers
branch: 64 registers
Reduction kernels also dropped from 46 to 40 registers.

ClimaAtmos with config/perf_configs/bm_aquaplanet_progedmf_1m.yml is essentially unchanged.
title: Optimize GPU DataLayout indexing with linear striding and singleton broadcasting
